Today we got more proof that our economy isn’t working for most people. A few huge corporations, including Amazon, announced tens of thousands of job cuts… and their stock prices kept going up. Because artificial intelligence and automation are already having a massive impact.  And stock markets in general hit record highs… but so did car repossessions. Because there is a massive divergence in our economy. The stock market doesn’t reflect the economy that most Americans are experiencing.

When voters talk to me about AI in this district, I hear a version of the same thing: nobody asked us. It showed up in our kids' phones, in the hiring process, in our electric bills, and there's no one in charge of it. [...] It’s important that the United States continue leading the world in AI development, but we need to make sure it’s developed safely and works for people, not just tech companies and billionaires.

We should do everything we can to get the benefits of AI – from new and faster cures for disease to less time wasted – without massive lay-offs, letting ourselves be helpless in the face of algorithms that addict our kids to AI-created content that makes it hard to know truth from lies, or a data center buildout that drives up electricity costs for families. We need guardrails. And we need to protect workers.

Congress should act quickly to establish a federal framework for AI that includes clear standards for transparency and testing. That will require increased investment in the Center for AI Standards and Innovation to ensure that the federal government has the capacity to test & evaluate models for safety and alignment.

Congress should also take action to maintain our international lead in AI development, because winning the AI race doesn't mean running it without rules, it means being the country that writes them. [...] This is where we are with frontier AI right now, which is why we need to strengthen our export controls so advanced computer chips don’t fall into the wrong hands. And we need to treat the theft of frontier AI models like a national security threat by requiring labs to strengthen their security to government-grade standards.

We’ve watched as social media has harmed a generation of kids’ mental health, and we can’t let the same happen with AI chatbots. I’d be proud to join Sen. Blumenthal in pushing for the GUARD Act, which would bar minors from accessing chatbots and mandate disclosure that chatbots aren’t humans or licensed professionals. We cannot allow AI companies to put their bottom lines before kids’ wellbeing.
As artificial intelligence comes at us fast, it’s more important than ever that every single child in America is prepared to be a strong critical thinker.
We need to be honest about the fact that [AI is] going to turn a lot of things upside down, on jobs, on what our kids are exposed to,

This is one reason the economy feels broken: Over the last forty years, the share of national income going to corporate profits has gone up — a lot. And the share going to workers’ pay and benefits has gone down — a lot. This is likely to get worse, AI productivity gains just concentrate wealth more. We already have a country that feels like it’s got two economies. But if we don’t start rebalancing, including through a fair tax policy, to economy that most Americans experience is going to feel more and more broken.
